title: Dissipation-enhanced vortex clustering in a compressible quantum fluid
authors: P. Comaron, M. Matuszewski, D. Sanvitto, D. Ballarini, A. S. Lanotte
abstract: Vortex clustering is commonly associated with conservative two-dimensional quantum-fluid dynamics. Therefore, particle loss is mainly expected to limit clustering by shortening the time available for vortex correlations to develop. Here we show instead that particle loss can enhance transient vortex clustering beyond the conservative evolution. We numerically study freely decaying, confined two-dimensional condensates initialized with random distributions of vortices and antivortices, and find a pronounced nonmonotonic dependence of the maximum clustering on particle lifetime. The enhancement is strongest at intermediate particle-loss rates, where loss-induced background rarefaction and incompressible kinetic energy relaxation occur on comparable timescales. Our results identify a finite dynamical window, selected by linear particle loss, in which a confined compressible quantum fluid develops stronger same-sign vortex correlations than in the conservative limit.
summary: This paper demonstrates that particle loss (dissipation) does not merely limit vortex clustering in a quantum fluid; instead, it actively enhances it beyond what is possible in conservative systems. The enhancement peaks at intermediate decay rates because this regime allows background rarefaction and kinetic energy relaxation to compete constructively with vortex correlation development.
main_problem: The study investigates how particle loss (dissipation) affects vortex clustering dynamics in a compressible quantum fluid, specifically determining if dissipation can enhance ordering beyond the purely conservative limit.
main_result: Dissipation enhances transient vortex clustering significantly at intermediate particle-loss rates, establishing a finite dynamical window where correlations are stronger than in the conservative case.
method: The research employs numerical simulations solving the dissipative Gross-Pitaevskii equation (dGPE) for freely decaying, confined condensates initialized with random vortices and antivortices.
model_or_system: The system is a two-dimensional compressible quantum fluid modeled by the dGPE incorporating linear particle loss ($\gamma$). The dynamics are studied using parameters relevant to exciton-polariton condensates.
key_observables: Maximum mean vortex correlation ($C_{\max}$), temporal evolution of $\langle C(t) angle$ and $N_v(t)$, and the decay rates/components of total, kinetic, and interaction energy.
important_parameters: Particle lifetime ($	au_\gamma$), which dictates a nonmonotonic dependence on clustering efficiency; intermediate loss rates are optimal for enhancement.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes linear particle losses ($\gamma$) and models the system using the dGPE framework, comparing results against the conservative limit ($\gamma=0$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the non-monotonic dependence of clustering on $	au_\gamma$, energy decay pathways showing competition between kinetic and interaction components, and phase portraits comparing dissipative vs. conservative ordering.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the effect of dissipation on vortex correlations, first establishing the enhancement mechanism via $C_{\max}$ vs. $	au_\gamma$. It then delves into the underlying energy dynamics, decomposing total energy decay to show how kinetic and interaction energies evolve differently under loss compared to conservative evolution.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it explores non-equilibrium dynamics in quantum fluids, showing that dissipation can drive complex ordering phenomena by selecting optimal timescales rather than simply truncating the process. This has implications for understanding decoherence effects on superfluid order.
